noFix.default: This issue requires manual review and cannot be fixed automatically. Follow the guidance in the Suggestion column.
noFix.RV001: The file could not be read because of an encoding error. In Excel, use Save As → CSV UTF-8, or use Notepad Save As → UTF-8, then upload the file again.
noFix.RV002: The file contains no data rows. Check the file contents and upload it again.
noFix.RV003: Duplicate column names are present. Rename duplicate columns in Excel (for example, Blood Pressure → Systolic BP and Blood Pressure.1 → Diastolic BP), then upload the file again.
noFix.RV101: The target variable (the outcome to predict) is missing. If an outcome column exists but was not detected, mark it as Label/Event in Column Profiles below; otherwise, add an outcome column in Excel.
noFix.RV102: Adding recommended fields such as age and sex is suggested but not required. Add these columns in Excel to support stratified analysis.
noFix.RV302: Date formats are inconsistent. The platform will standardize them to YYYY-MM-DD automatically; no manual fix is needed.
noFix.RV502: Values are outside the clinically plausible range. Manually check whether this is a unit error or a true extreme value. Verify the unit (for example, mg/dL vs mmol/L) or correct entry errors in Excel.
noFix.RV601: Too many categories may indicate an ID column or free text. If this is an ID column, click Drop Column; if it must be retained, consider merging similar categories.
noFix.RV701: Class imbalance is a data characteristic. The platform will automatically use class weights and PR-AUC; no manual fix is needed.
noFix.RV801: This is a long-table structure (one record per row) and must be converted to a wide table (one row per patient). Use an Excel pivot table or the upcoming platform wizard.
noFix.RV803: The same test uses multiple units and they must be standardized. Convert values with a formula in Excel (for example, mmol/L × 18 = mg/dL), or wait for the platform's unit standardization feature.
noFix.RV804: Extreme values require manual review. They may be unit errors (extra zeros) or entry errors; check the maximum and minimum values in Excel.
noFix.RV705: Possible repeated records for the same patient. Confirm whether these are normal repeat visits or duplicate entries that should be removed.

quality.fixCreatesVersion: The fix will create a new file version in the original dataset directory. Your uploaded source file will not be changed. You can also skip automatic fixing, edit the source file manually, and upload it again.

fixRisk.drop_column: This column will be permanently removed from the new version, and its data cannot be recovered from that version. Use only for columns confirmed to be unnecessary.
fixRisk.drop_duplicates: Fully duplicated rows will be deleted and only one copy retained. If duplicates are genuine records, samples will be lost.
fixRisk.to_missing: Unrecognized values will be set to missing, and the original values cannot be recovered from the new version.
fixRisk.remap_semantic: The column's semantic role will be relabeled, affecting task detection and validation results.
fixRisk.rename_column: The column will be renamed. Make sure the new name does not conflict with an existing column.
fixRisk.pivot_long_to_wide: The long table will be converted to a wide table (one row per patient). Duplicate values will be averaged, causing a major structural change.
fixRisk.winsorize_outliers: Outliers will be clipped to the 1st and 99th percentiles. Extreme values will be modified but not deleted.
fixRisk.impute_missing: Missing values will be filled automatically (median for numeric columns and mode for categorical columns). The original missing state cannot be recovered.
fixRisk.drop_rows_with_pattern: Rows matching the specified pattern will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
fixRisk.normalize_units: Units will be standardized and the original units and values will be changed.

quality.executeCreatesVersion: The fix will create a new file version and automatically rerun validation. The source file will not be changed.
